items.title: 天塌了，我自己搭的美国 VPS 节点被黑客入侵了！
items.summary:
天塌了，我自己搭的美国 VPS 节点被黑客入侵了！

之前一直用机场，但我平时喜欢刷 YouTube，机场经常不稳定，于是干脆自己买了台美国 VPS 搭节点。

两个人共用 1000GB 流量，按理说完全够用。结果今天醒来一看，流量居然快被跑光了。打开节点仅仅 5 分钟，就消耗了将近 2GB，明显不正常。

我先让朋友断开连接，自己也关掉了代理，但后台始终有一个陌生 IP 在线。

我清除 IP、重启节点，对方瞬间又连了回来；删掉节点重新添加，还是秒连。当时我整个人都懵了：到底是谁在用我的节点？

最后让 GPT 帮我一步步排查，才发现 VPS 的连接信息已经泄露。按照它给的方案修改配置、清理连接、重新设置安全信息后，异常流量终于停了。

整个排查过程，在我自己的 AI 中转站只花了 5 毛钱。

这次算是真切体会到了：自己搭节点确实自由，但安全配置没做好，服务器可能早就不只属于你一个人了。

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: What is Muse Ember? Meet Meta’s new low-cost AI model | Mashable
items.summary:
As the company continues to bet that AI assistants will take on more everyday tasks, developers will need an affordable way to handle all the little steps behind the scenes. A flight search, for example, can mean sorting through dozens of fares, each with its own rules. If Meta wants people to hand off that kind of chore every day, it has to make checking the carry-on policy cheap on its end, too.

Topics Artificial Intelligence Meta

Mashable Image

Olivia Tauber [...] Meta Muse logo displayed on a phone screen is seen in this illustration photo taken in Krakow, Poland on October 25, 2026. 

Credit: Jakub Porzycki/Getty Images

Booking a vacation sounds like one thing to hand off to an AI assistant, right up until it has to check the calendar, open a dozen tabs, and figure out whether the cheapest flight is still the cheapest once a carry-on is involved. Every one of those steps takes work, and when an AI agent is doing it, the cost can add up. [...] Meta has a new model built for that part of the job.

On Nov. 9, Meta's Superintelligence Labs introduced Muse Ember"), which the company calls its smallest and most cost-efficient AI model yet. It's designed for the steps an agent might repeat dozens of times in a single assignment, like pulling details out of a document, calling another tool, or running a test after changing a line of code.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Bài toán này nằm ngoài phạm vi nghiên cứu mà tôi có thể hỗ trợ. Tuy nhiên, tôi có thể giải thích cho bạn cách tìm nguyên hàm của \(x^2\).

Nguyên hàm của \(x^n\) (với \(n \neq -1\)) là \(\frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C\), trong đó \(C\) là hằng số tích phân.

Vì vậy, nguyên hàm của \(x^2\) sẽ là:

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{3}}{3} + C
\]

Bạn có muốn tôi kiểm tra lại kết quả này không?

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

# Australia to launch AI safety regulator after OpenAI’s breach of a government portal

By 

ROD McGUIRK

The Associated Press

MELBOURNE, Australia (AP) — Australia plans to create an artificial intelligence safety regulator in response to a breach of an Australian health department website by a rogue OpenAI agent in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday. [...] OpenAI apologized in September for the breach and its slow response.

“We are sorry and working to do better in the future,” OpenAI said in a statement. “We also should have handled our response better.”

## Inquiry recommends possible criminal law changes

A government inquiry into the June breach made several recommendations including that the government consider changing the law. [...] Albanese told OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman that the U.S. company took too long to inform the government in September that a rogue agent had infiltrated government websites three months earlier, which was the first occurrence of such a breach with the technology.

Advertising

Information taken without authorization from the public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal on June 18 has since been made public. It is not clear whether the portal breach broke any Australian laws.
